newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower after weaker ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower after weaker ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were expected to open lower Tuesday following a weaker ACCESS session, industry sources said.
May over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.03 to $2.04 after settling Monday at $2.064 per million British thermal units (mmBtu).
May, set to expire Thursday, last traded in ACCESS 2.4 cents lower at $2.04.
"We're getting progressively lower highs...The locals may try to drive it lower," one market source said, noting early cash at Henry Hub was quoted mostly steady at $2.06-2.09.

Traders pegged near-support in May at $2.035, with further buying likely at $1.925, $1.88, $1.85 and $1.825. Key resistance was seen at $2.095, the intraday high from March 10, with a break above that level probably triggering a move to about $2.16.

In Monday's cash market, Gulf Coast prices were steady to down slightly at about $2.05. Midcontinent pipes showed similar movement to the low-to-mid $1.90s. Gas at the New York city gate fell by about five cents to the mid-to-high $2.30s.
Lending some support to the market were forecasts calling for more below-normal temperatures throughout the Northeast, Midwest and northern Texas through this week.
Early expectations for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report are about 14-30 bcf of injections, versus a 27 bcf gain a year ago.
